- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices; apply 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model exhibits lagged reaction; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 periods ahead.
